summary: Entrywise, [P_t, X]_ij = (1_{w_i≥t} − 1_{w_j≥t})X_ij and (P_tX)_ii = 1_{w_i≥t}X_ii; summing over t ∈ (−a, a] counts the integers t between w_j and w_i (giving |w_i − w_j|) and those in (−a, w_i] (giving w_i + a). (intro_lines 18–20 are not proof: they are the rest of the statement, lines 18–20 by the statement-boundary overlay of a second-reader message; the line census takes the `:=` of `letI a :=` for the start of the value.)

steps.claim: −a ≤ w_i ≤ a for every i, with a = Σ_j|w_j|.

steps.lean:
simp [frobenius_norm_sq_eq_sum, coordProj, lie_def,
    trace, (Ioc ..).sum_comm, ite_sub, sub_ite,
    apply_ite norm, ← Order.lt_add_one_iff]; simp [sum_ite, ← add_mul,
    ← Ico_add_one_add_one_eq_Ioc, -Order.lt_add_one_iff, -Order.add_one_le_iff]
steps.claim: Expand both identities entrywise: the Frobenius norm as Σ_{i,j}|·|², [P_t, X]_ij = (1_{w_i ≥ t} − 1_{w_j ≥ t})·X_ij, the trace as Σ_i; exchange the sums over t and over (i, j), and rewrite the inner sums over t as the numbers of integers t ∈ (−a, a] with exactly one of w_i ≥ t, w_j ≥ t (first identity) and with t ≤ w_i (second identity).
Both counts are evaluated using step 1: the integers t ∈ (−a, a] lying between min(w_i, w_j) (exclusive) and max(w_i, w_j) (inclusive) are |w_i − w_j| many, and those with t ≤ w_i are w_i + a many.
